definition: One-shot learning is a problem setup in machine learning which leverages a singular example to assist with classification, originating in the field of computer vision to assist with object categorization.
details: Whereas most machine learning classification methods require training on hundreds or thousands of examples, one-shot learning aims to classify objects from one example. Few-shot learning is used for similar methods which utilize more than one example to assist with classification.
story: Imagine an art restorer who can spot a single cracked tile in a vast mosaic. What your eyes do without thinking, the machine does one careful layer at a time. The machine learns to see the way we do — starting with shapes and edges, then building up to whole objects and faces. The model looks the way you look at a crowd and finds the one face you know. That pixel-to-meaning climb is One-shot learning (computer vision).
